statement: A butterfly picture looks exactly the same on both sides of its middle line. Its left wing has 3 big spots and 2 small spots. How many spots does the whole butterfly have?

choices.misconception: I counted the spots on the left wing only.
I doubled the big spots and forgot about the small spots.
I doubled the small spots but counted the big spots only once.
I doubled the big spots but counted the small spots only once.

hints: What does the right wing look like?
Looking the same on both sides of a line means the right wing is a mirror copy of the left wing, with the same spots. Count one wing, then add its copy.
The left wing has 3 + 2 = 5 spots, and the right wing has the same number.

solutions.reliable: The right wing is a mirror copy of the left, so it also has 3 big and 2 small spots. Each wing has 5 spots, so the butterfly has 5 + 5 = 10. The idea to keep: a shape with a line of symmetry has two matching halves, so count one half and double it.

whyOnTest: Line symmetry means two matching halves, and doubling only part of one half is the slip this catches.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
